proof_nl:
Let n>1 be an integer, x a real number, and z an integer. By definition,
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor n(x+z)\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor k(x+z)\rfloor}{k}.
Since nz and kz are integers for every k, we use the standard floor identity \lfloor t+m\rfloor=\lfloor t\rfloor+m for any real t and integer m. Hence
\lfloor n(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor nx+nz\rfloor=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz,
and for each k,
\lfloor k(x+z)\rfloor=\lfloor kx+kz\rfloor=\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz.
Substituting these into the definition gives
E(n,x+z)=\bigl(\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz\bigr)-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor+kz}{k}.
Distributing the sum,
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nz-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{kz}{k}.
Because \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{kz}{k}=\sum_{k=1}^n z=nz, the nz terms cancel, leaving
E(n,x+z)=\lfloor nx\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}=E(n,x).
Therefore E(n,x+z)=E(n,x) for every real x and every integer z.
solver_summary: Use the floor identity floor(t+m)=floor(t)+m for integer m on each term after shifting x by an integer z; the added nz terms cancel exactly.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly establishes integer-shift invariance of E(n,x) by applying the floor identity to nx and kx for each integer k, then canceling the added nz terms in the sum. The argument is complete and matches the lemma statement exactly.
